title: Tiered Serving Bundles — Validation Playground & OKR Mapping
creator: Leah Martinez
description:
Summary: Build and validate a set of composable, tiered 'serving bundles' (combinations of batching parameters, KV cache TTLs, and quantization profiles) and a Validation Playground that lets product, SRE, and EconOps run controlled experiments to measure latency, token cost, and quality impact. The goal is to map bundles to customer usage patterns and an OKR-driven rollout plan that safely delivers unit-cost savings without material quality regressions.

Context: We have numerous one-off experiments for batching, KV prefilling, and dynamic quantization. Teams need a repeatable way to assemble these levers into named bundles, run validation jobs against canonical prompt sets and synthetic workloads, and export metrics to the savings dashboard and the rollout engine. This initiative formalizes bundles and provides an interactive playground + automation for validation and OKR reporting.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 initial bundles (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) with exact knob values for batching, cache TTL, and quant profile
Validation Playground runs reproducible experiments and outputs latency (p50/p95), token cost delta, and quality regression delta for each bundle
OKR mapping doc that ties bundles to measurable targets: cost reduction %, latency SLO impact, and quality guardrails
Automated export to Cost Dashboard (savings estimate) and to Rollout Engine for canary gating
progress_updates: 2025-11-11 - Leah M: Kickoff with Eng and SRE; agreed on canonical workload set and initial metric schema.
2025-11-13 - Omar C: Prototype playground UI wireframe reviewed; ENG requested API contract for experiment runs (ENG-19877).
2025-11-15 - Priya Singh (EconOps): Ran first synthetic sweep across batching window and observed 8-11% token savings for Balanced config; added quality checks for hallucination rate.
2025-11-17 - Eng team (Ben R): Basic automation for artifact capture (latency traces + token counts) landed in GH PR #1128; integration tests failing intermittently under long sequences.
2025-11-18 - PM review: Prioritized hardening of long-sequence tracing and a new sub-issue to add cost-estimate margin of error reporting (PM-536415).
risks: Aggressive quantization could cause subtle quality regressions not detected by current eval sets
Autoscaling interactions: high batching may increase P95 under bursty traffic
Rollout complexity: multiple bundles increases surface area for RBAC/feature flags errors
next_steps: Stabilize artifact capture for long-sequence runs (ENG-20102) — blocker for conservative regression checks
Expand prompt/eval set to include business-critical customer prompts provided by Solutions Eng (data ingestion gated by NDA)
Finish UI -> API glue for interactive Playground and enable 'replay' mode for historical experiment runs
Create OKR dashboard tile with bundle-to-OKR mapping and link to rollout gating checks
notes: This ticket intentionally separates feature definition (bundles) from rollout automation. We expect 2 sprints of validation before proposing default bundle for self-serve accounts. Stakeholders: Product, EconOps, Serving/Runtime, SRE, Solutions.
